page.title: Workspace
page.purpose: Let an operator review repository state, inspect diffs, compose commits, and move between history and scenario review without losing context.

priorities.statement: Repository status and branch context stay visible before any mutating action.
The active file diff is the primary work surface on desktop.
Changes, diff, commit, history, and review remain reachable as equivalent full-page tabs on mobile.
Desktop operators can resize and rearrange supporting panels without hiding the primary diff.
Mobile chrome stays pinned and safely tappable at the device edge.

states.description: Repository workspace loaded with status chrome, panel navigation, and the primary review surface.
Initial health and repository status requests are in flight.
A git operation or status request failed and is surfaced as a toast.
A previous commit is selected; the file list and diff inspect that commit instead of the working tree.
Settings modal exposes layout, grouping, credential, and health configuration.

elements.description: The full Git Control Tower application surface.
Desktop status chrome with branch, sync, health, review, search, settings, and refresh controls.
Mobile status chrome with branch, sync, review, search, and menu controls.
Mobile bottom navigation across Changes, Diff, Commit, History, and Review panels.

elements.name: Changes
elements.description: Mobile tab that opens the file-change panel as the current page.

elements.name: Diff
elements.description: Mobile tab that opens the diff panel as the current page.

elements.name: Commit
elements.description: Mobile tab that opens commit composition as the current page.

elements.name: History
elements.description: Mobile tab that opens git history as the current page.

elements.name: Review
elements.description: Mobile tab that opens the scenario review surface as the current page.
Working-tree file list with staging and grouping controls.
Primary diff or source viewer for the selected file.
Commit message, validation, push, and pre-commit controls.

elements.name: Scenario review
elements.description: Chrome entry point into scenario review.
Chrome entry point into file search.

claims.statement: Desktop chrome exposes review, search, and settings actions without opening a menu.
Desktop status chrome is visible without page scrolling.
Desktop branch/status chrome reads before review, search, and settings actions.
Mobile status chrome remains visible without page scrolling.
The mobile workspace exposes the same core work surfaces through bottom-nav tabs.
Every mobile bottom-nav tab is keyboard reachable.
Mobile bottom navigation is visible without scrolling to the end of the document.
Desktop support panels can be resized and rearranged without unmounting the active diff.
claims.rationale: The existing checker can prove panel presence and viewport visibility; drag-resize behavior needs a workflow-backed interaction check.

claims.statement: On mobile, each bottom-nav choice presents its panel as the full available page rather than shrinking the desktop split-pane layout.
claims.rationale: The current matrix captures only the default selected mobile tab; tab-switch state setup is the next interaction-runner step.

regions.note: Desktop support panels are user-resizable and can move left/right/bottom.
At mobile width, these same panels become full-page tabs controlled by mobile-nav.

x-responsive-transform.desktop: Resizable support panels surround the primary diff surface.
x-responsive-transform.mobile: The same surfaces are selected one at a time through pinned bottom navigation.
x-responsive-transform.schema-note: scenario-experience-spec/v1 expresses this through viewport-scoped claims plus open-world x- documentation; no schema change was required.
